</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.3.2. </span>Grounding via Agentic Exploration</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Guided by <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> initiates an agentic process to resolve implementation ambiguities within <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> by transitioning over the action space <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> through a sequence of states <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each new state is determined based on the prior history <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{&lt;t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{&lt;t}</annotation></semantics></math> and the accumulated observations <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{&lt;t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{&lt;t}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(5)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H_{t}=p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathcal{A},\mathcal{G},H_{&lt;t},O_{&lt;t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}=p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathcal{A},\mathcal{G},H_{&lt;t},O_{&lt;t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Profiling</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To resolve uncertainties regarding value distributions and data formats, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> autonomously generates exploratory queries <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{exp,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{exp,t}</annotation></semantics></math> at iteration <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. To prevent large result sets from flooding the context window, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> automatically compresses extensive outputs into a statistical summary <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{t}=\sigma(\text{Exec}(Q_{exp,t},\mathcal{D}^{*}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext>Exec</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{t}=\sigma(\text{Exec}(Q_{exp,t},\mathcal{D}^{*}))</annotation></semantics></math>, providing a compact yet comprehensive view of the data landscape.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Consolidation</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As multi-step exploration progresses, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> performs periodic state compression to prevent context saturation and maintain logical coherence as evidence accumulates. Once sufficient observations are collected, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> synthesizes a consolidated status update that aligns observations with the overall logical plan and refines its understanding of schema semantics.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">SQL Synthesis</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After all implementation details are grounded in empirical evidence, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> synthesizes a candidate SQL query <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> that maps the refined reasoning state onto the physical database syntax. The synthesized query is immediately validated against the database environment to ensure execution feasibility. If the execution <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Exec}(S,\mathcal{D}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Exec</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Exec}(S,\mathcal{D}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> returns an error, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> leverages the resulting feedback to drive self-correction in subsequent iterations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Confirmation</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following a successful execution, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> enters a terminal state to perform secondary verification of semantic fidelity. Specifically, <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> evaluates whether the SQL logic aligns with the user requirements, the accumulated observations, and the latest logical plan. The output is finalized only after <span id="S3.SS3.SSS2.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> confirms these conditions, thereby preventing logical drift during the multi-step generation process.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our evaluation focuses on the effectiveness of schema linking in reducing the search space while preserving relevant columns, and the downstream execution accuracy of the generated SQL queries.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1. </span>Datasets</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">BIRD-Dev.</span> The development set of BIRD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023a</a>)</cite>, which is a large-scale cross-domain dataset consists of 1,534 queries across 11 databases. It requires the model to resolve ambiguities in fine-grained schema details, such as similarly named columns or dirty database values.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spider 2.0-Snow.</span> Spider 2.0 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lei et al., 2024</a>)</cite> represents the frontier of enterprise-level Text-to-SQL tasks. Its primary challenge lies in its massive schema size, featuring an average of over 800 columns per database and highly complex SQL structures. We focus on the Spider 2.0-Snow sub-task, which requires generating SQL queries in the Snowflake dialect, a standard for modern cloud data warehouses.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2. </span>Experiment 1: Schema Linking Performance</h3>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.1. </span>Metrics</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate schema linking as a retrieval task, aiming to identify the minimal sufficient subgraph required for the query. We follow prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> to report the following metrics:</p>
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Strict Recall Rate (SRR)</span> measures the percentage of queries where the retrieved schema fully covers the ground truth. We consider SRR the most important metric, as it directly determines whether downstream SQL generation is possible to succeed.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Non-Strict Recall (NSR) computes the proportion of required columns retrieved, even if the full subgraph is incomplete.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Non-Strict Precision (NSP) measures the ratio of relevant columns in the retrieved set, reflecting the model’s ability to filter noise.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Non-Strict F1-Score (NSF) is the harmonic mean of NSR and NSP, offering a holistic view of retrieval quality.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.2. </span>Experimental Setup</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure a rigorous evaluation, we define specific testing splits and model backbones for each dataset.
For BIRD-Dev, we use a widely adopted subset of 147 cases <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Talaei et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., [n. d.]</a>)</cite> to evaluate the performance of DeepSeek-V3.2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite> as the backbone, allowing us to test the model’s capability within a controlled range and replicate more baselines. For full-set evaluation, we use Qwen3-32B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
For Spider 2.0-Snow, we utilize GPT-4.1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Achiam et al., 2023</a>)</cite> on the 120-case subset with official golden SQLs<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
                
                
                
              Full execution ground truth is available, but golden SQLs cover only 120 cases.</span></span></span>, selected for its extended context window, which ensures both baseline and our method are not limited by context window size when processing Spider 2.0’s larger schema.
Ground truth columns are obtained by using both GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek-V3.2 to extract referenced columns from the golden SQLs, followed by manual verification.
The instruction templates <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{plan}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{plan}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{agg}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{agg}</annotation></semantics></math> in Equ. <a href="#S3.E1" title="In 3.2.1. Hypothesis Generation via Logical Planning ‣ 3.2. Agentic Exploration for Schema Linking ‣ 3. Methodology ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{del}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{del}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{sel}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{sel}</annotation></semantics></math> in Equ. <a href="#S3.E2" title="In 3.2.2. Search Space Reduction via Dual-Pathway Pruning ‣ 3.2. Agentic Exploration for Schema Linking ‣ 3. Methodology ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{semantics}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{semantics}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{exp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{exp}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{final}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{final}</annotation></semantics></math> in Equ. <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.2.3. Hypothesis Verification via Agentic Exploration ‣ 3.2. Agentic Exploration for Schema Linking ‣ 3. Methodology ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> are provided in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Instruction Templates ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.3. </span>Baselines</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare our approach against comprehensive baselines, including CodeS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024b</a>)</cite> and RESDSQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2023b</a>)</cite>, which are training-base methods, and TA-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, RSL-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, ReFoRCE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al., [n. d.]</a>)</cite>, DSR-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hao et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and AutoLink <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, which are training-free methods.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.4. </span>Results on Schema Linking</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.3.1. Guidance via Deterministic Retrieval ‣ 3.3. Agentic Exploration for SQL Generation ‣ 3. Methodology ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> presents the schema linking performance across two benchmarks and three experimental settings. <span id="S4.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> achieves the highest SRR across all settings, recording 97.28% on the BIRD subset, 87.68% on the BIRD full set, and 88.33% on Spider 2.0-Snow.
We observe that existing training-based methods perform poorly on Spider 2.0, with significant drops in SRR. Among training-free methods, although TA-SQL, ReFoRCE, and DSR-SQL (on Spider 2.0) achieve higher NSP, their SRR is much lower than ours (e.g., ReFoRCE achieves 35.00% on Spider 2.0), rendering them unsuitable for downstream SQL generation, where missing columns can lead to critical errors.
While AutoLink achieves an SRR close to ours on the BIRD subset and Spider 2.0, its NSP is noticeably lower, highlighting the superiority of <span id="S4.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> in maintaining precision while maximizing recall.
Furthermore, <span id="S4.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> better adapts to weaker models, whereas AutoLink shows a significant drop in SRR on the BIRD full set (with Qwen3-32B).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.5. </span>Schema Linking Details</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Logical Planning: We sample <math id="S4.SS2.SSS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=2</annotation></semantics></math> paths at temperature 0.8 using only the query <math id="S4.SS2.SSS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> as input, then aggregate them at temperature 0.2.
Dual-Pathway Pruning: Columns are batched by table to maintain semantic integrity, with each batch constrained to 8–12k tokens. To minimize API overhead, we implement <span id="S4.SS2.SSS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Schema Merging</span>: tables with identical columns are consolidated into a single prompt entry that displays one representative schema alongside a list of all matching table names.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2. </span>Execution accuracy on BIRD-Dev (<math id="S4.T2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1534" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1534</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1534</annotation></semantics></math>) across difficulty levels. Results marked with <sup id="S4.T2.3" class="ltx_sup">∗</sup> are locally reproduced, while others are collected from existing literature. <section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3. </span>Experiment 2: SQL Generation Performance</h3>

<section id="S4.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.3.1. </span>Metrics</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Execution Accuracy (EX)</span> as the evaluation metric, measuring the percentage of generated queries that return the exact result set as the ground truth<span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">3</span>
                
                
                
              Compared to BIRD, Spider 2.0 adopts a relaxed evaluation protocol due to output format ambiguity in complex queries, tolerating irrelevant columns in the result set.</span></span></span>. In addition, following prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al., [n. d.]</a>)</cite>, we also report <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pass@8</span> on Spider 2.0-Snow, where a question is considered solved if at least one correct SQL appears among eight candidates. Unless specified otherwise, we use the results reported in the official papers of the respective baselines.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.3.2. </span>Baselines</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare <span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> against open-source methods or those that have been reproduced by other works. For <span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">BIRD-Dev</span>, we benchmark against C3-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dong et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, DAIL-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, TA-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, MAG-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, SuperSQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, MAC-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, Contextual-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Agrawal and Nguyen, 2025</a>)</cite>, MCS-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, RSL-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, CHESS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Talaei et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, DSR-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hao et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, AutoLink <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, and OpenSearch-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. For <span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spider 2.0-Snow</span>, we compare against Spider-Agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lei et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, ReFoRCE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al., [n. d.]</a>)</cite>, and DSR-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hao et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3. </span>Main results on Spider 2.0-Snow (<math id="S4.T3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=547" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>547</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=547</annotation></semantics></math>), evaluating execution accuracy (EX), solution coverage (Pass@8), and average token consumption. <math id="S4.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> denotes number of votes. <td id="S4.T4.8.10.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:7.3pt;padding-right:7.3pt;"><math id="S4.T4.m50" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79.17_{{\color[rgb]{0.7539,0,0}\downarrow 1.66}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>79.17</mn><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#C00000;" mathcolor="#C00000" stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#C00000;" mathcolor="#C00000">1.66</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79.17_{{\color[rgb]{0.7539,0,0}\downarrow 1.66}}</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.3.3. </span>Result Analysis</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As presented in Tables <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.2.5. Schema Linking Details ‣ 4.2. Experiment 1: Schema Linking Performance ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3.2. Baselines ‣ 4.3. Experiment 2: SQL Generation Performance ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> consistently outperforms mainstream approaches.
On <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">BIRD-Dev</span>, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> achieves <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">70.7%</span> accuracy, surpassing retrieval-augmented methods like DAIL-SQL (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="54.3\%_{\downarrow 16.4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>54.3</mn><mo>%</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>16.4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.3\%_{\downarrow 16.4}</annotation></semantics></math>) and RSL-SQL (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="67.2\%_{\downarrow 3.5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>67.2</mn><mo>%</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>3.5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">67.2\%_{\downarrow 3.5}</annotation></semantics></math>). Despite slightly trailing DSR-SQL in the <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Challenging</span> subset, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> dominates the <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Simple</span> and <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Moderate</span> categories, demonstrating superior robustness against semantic ambiguity.
This advantage extends to <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spider 2.0-Snow</span>, where <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> achieves <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">51.01%</span> with DeepSeek-R1, exceeding DSR-SQL (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="35.28\%_{\downarrow 15.73\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>35.28</mn><mo>%</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mrow><mn>15.73</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35.28\%_{\downarrow 15.73\%}</annotation></semantics></math>) and ReFORCE with o3 (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="35.83\%_{\downarrow 15.18\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>35.83</mn><mo>%</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mrow><mn>15.18</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35.83\%_{\downarrow 15.18\%}</annotation></semantics></math>).
Notably, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> attains a Pass@8 of <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">70.20%</span>, nearly doubling ReFoRCE-o3 (39.85%), indicating that our guided exploration effectively maximizes solution coverage.
Additionally, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> optimizes token consumption, using fewer tokens (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18k\cdot v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18k\cdot v</annotation></semantics></math>) than ReFoRCE (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23k\cdot v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23k\cdot v</annotation></semantics></math>) on Spider 2.0, and only 3.7k tokens per query with superior accuracy on BIRD (Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Token Consumption Analysis ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>).
The comparison with DSR-SQL further highlights <span id="S4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span>’s superiority: while DSR-SQL incorporates data profiling in SQL generation process, it lacks agentic exploration in the schema linking phase and guidance for exploration, achieving only 35.28% EX.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.3.4. </span>SQL Generation Details</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement all agentic components in a training-free manner, with detailed instructions provided in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Instruction Templates ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.
Guidance Retrieval: We map inferred natural language paths to the library <math id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> (provided in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Tip Library Details ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>) using keyword matching, which achieved <math id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;95\%</annotation></semantics></math> recall in pilot tests on a BIRD-train subset.
Data Profiling: The profiling function <math id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> compresses result sets exceeding 30 rows into the top 10 rows plus statistics (row count, cardinality, types, and NULL ratios). For each question, we enforce a limit of 40 actions and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="56k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>56</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">56k</annotation></semantics></math> tokens; a mandatory SQL synthesis action is triggered at 38 actions or 52k tokens. For Spider 2.0-Snow cases with external knowledge (up to <math id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30k</annotation></semantics></math> tokens), we pre-filter the documentation for query-relevant snippets using the tested model (Appx. <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Instruction Templates ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>).
Context Management: During consolidation, we prune the interaction history to retain only exploratory queries, execution results, and the latest consolidated plan/understanding.
Inference: We sample 8 candidates per task. For BIRD, we select the final answer using a reward model following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Agrawal and Nguyen, 2025</a>)</cite>. For Spider 2.0-Snow, we use result-based majority voting with model selection (Appx. <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Instruction Templates ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>) as a tie-breaker.
The instruction <math id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sql}_{kw}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sql}_{kw}</annotation></semantics></math> for generating SQL realization paths, and the definition of the Action space <math id="S4.SS3.SSS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> are also provided in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Instruction Templates ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4. </span>Analysis</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we present a series of experiments analyzing the impact of autonomous exploration, the scalability of test-time compute, and the contributions of core components in both the schema linking and SQL generation stages. We also present a case study in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Case Study ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.
All experiments are conducted on the Spider 2.0-Snow subset, which includes official golden SQLs.
We prioritize this benchmark due to its higher complexity, which provides more discriminative metrics, effectively highlighting the performance boundaries of different strategies.
For SQL generation-related investigations (Sections <a href="#S4.SS4.SSS1" title="4.4.1. Effect of Exploration ‣ 4.4. Analysis ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4.1</span></a> and <a href="#S4.SS4.SSS2" title="4.4.2. Test-Time Compute Scaling ‣ 4.4. Analysis ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4.2</span></a>), we consistently use the <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">oracle schema</span> setting, where models are provided with ground truth schema information. This approach isolates the impact of schema linking errors, ensuring that performance differences are attributed solely to SQL generation. We also introduce the <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EX@8</span> metric, which calculates the average EX score across 8 results.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.4.1. </span>Effect of Exploration</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To quantify the contribution of agentic exploration, we compare three settings: <span id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">w/ Exploration</span> (ours), <span id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">w/o Exploration</span> (pure SQL generation with execution-guided refinement), and <span id="S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Oracle Exploration<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
                  <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note"><span id="footnote4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">4</span></span>
                  
                  
                  
                <span id="footnote4.6" class="ltx_text">Oracle Exploration</span><span id="footnote4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> injects implementation details derived from Ground Truth SQL via GPT-5, including parsing strategies and implicit data handling steps that are not explicitly mentioned in the query or schema, such as how to join multiple tables.</span></span></span></span></span>.
Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.3.2. Baselines ‣ 4.3. Experiment 2: SQL Generation Performance ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> presents the results, revealing three critical insights:</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Exploration as a Performance Multiplier</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Exploration significantly improves performance across all metrics. For instance, DeepSeek-V3.2’s EX score increases from 39.17% to 57.50% (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>18.33%). This shows that reasoning alone cannot fully resolve the gap between abstract logic and physical data states—empirical verification is essential for generating accurate enterprise-level SQL queries.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The “Rich Get Richer” Effect</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We observe that exploration gains correlate with base model capability. Weaker models like GPT-4o show modest improvements (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>5.00% in EX), while stronger models such as DeepSeek-V3.2 and Gemini-3-Pro experience much larger gains (e.g., DeepSeek-V3.2 <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>18.33% in EX). This suggests that stronger models possess superior cognitive agility, allowing them to better formulate hypotheses, interpret exploration feedback, and synthesizing this information into more accurate SQL logic.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Autonomy vs. Oracle Guidance</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Comparing autonomous exploration (w/ Exploration) with Oracle Exploration reveals a capability-dependent trade-off. For weaker models like GPT-4o, Oracle guidance consistently improves all metrics (e.g., Pass@8 <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>6.67%), suggesting that models with limited reasoning capacity benefit more from shortcuts.
However, for stronger models, while Oracle improves EX, it often hurts Pass@8 (e.g., DeepSeek-V3.2 <math id="S4.SS4.SSS1.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>8.34%). This indicates that while Oracle narrows the search space, autonomous exploration provides a broader understanding of the data. For DeepSeek-V3.2 and Gemini-3-Pro, self-exploration even leads to higher EX@8 scores than Oracle, indicating that stronger models more consistently benefit from exploration.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.16720v1/passk_v2.png" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/277;" width="429" height="277" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3. </span>Performance scaling of GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3.2 on Spider 2.0-Snow subset (<math id="S4.F3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=120</annotation></semantics></math>) using the oracle schema.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.4.2. </span>Test-Time Compute Scaling</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To investigate the relationship between inference budget and performance scaling, we conduct a scalability analysis by performing <math id="S4.SS4.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=8</annotation></semantics></math> independent generation runs using the oracle schema.
Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Autonomy vs. Oracle Guidance ‣ 4.4.1. Effect of Exploration ‣ 4.4. Analysis ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> reveals three key insights:</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expanding Latent Potential</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The growth of Pass@k confirms that scaling test-time compute effectively expands the solution search space, uncovering the models’ latent reasoning potential. Notably, with a budget of <math id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=8</annotation></semantics></math>, the coverage of GPT-4o (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Pass@8=55.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>55.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Pass@8=55.8\%</annotation></semantics></math>) surpasses the average single-pass performance of DeepSeek-V3.2 (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EX@k=52.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>52.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EX@k=52.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>), suggesting that test-time compute scaling can effectively compensate for intrinsic model capabilities.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Performance Consistency &amp; The Selection Gap</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While Pass@k rises significantly, EX@k remains stable, suggesting high fidelity per trace rather than relying on brute-force sampling to rescue low-quality attempts.
However, a substantial gap persists between the potential maximum (Pass@k) and the voting result (EX). For instance, DeepSeek-V3.2 achieves 79.17 Pass@8, yet voting captures only 57.50. This highlights that while the generative capability is sufficient, <span id="S4.SS4.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">answer selection</span> remains a bottleneck.
In this work, we employ multiple sampling to mitigate generation variance rather than as a primary source of performance improvement, leaving the optimization of answer selection to future research.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5. </span>Ablation study on schema linking components. The evaluation is stratified into two stages: the <span id="S4.T5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pruning</span> Stage (top), measuring the quality of the intermediate candidate columns before verification, and the <span id="S4.T5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Verification Stage</span> (bottom), assessing the final output.
<math id="S4.T5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>C</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{C}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the average number of columns retained per query (3,430 before pruning).</figcaption>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.4.3. </span>Ablation Study on Schema Linking Components</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform an ablation study to evaluate the contributions of key components in schema linking. Results are shown in Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Performance Consistency &amp; The Selection Gap ‣ 4.4.2. Test-Time Compute Scaling ‣ 4.4. Analysis ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The Recall-Precision Trade-off.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We observe that our full method achieves lower precision (NSP) compared to baselines. We argue this behavior is accepted, as enterprise queries often allow for multiple valid solution paths. For instance, returning either <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">id</span> or <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">name</span> is acceptable for entity identification requirements. While ground truth SQL may select one, a robust schema linker must preserve all candidates to avoid irreversible pruning errors. As a result, we trade reduced precision for higher SRR, as missing a single critical column renders correct SQL generation impossible.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Logical Planning.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Removing <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Logical Planning</span> minimally impacts pruning stage SRR (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow 0.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mrow><mn>0.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow 0.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>) but notably affects final SRR (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow 5.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mrow><mn>5.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow 5.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>). This indicates that verbalizing query intent and constraints provides necessary context for the agent to correctly verify column roles during exploration, preventing false rejections of critical elements.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dual-Pathway Pruning.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the pruning stage, relying on <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Only Selection</span> or <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Only Deletion</span> reduces SRR by 4.2% and 16.7%, respectively. Standard selection misses subtle columns, while aggressive deletion discards necessary structural keys. Combining both pathways, our method achieves the highest SRR of 97.5%. We note that the average of 383 retained columns corresponds to about 7<math id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, which fits well within the context window for verification.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Agentic Verification.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The bottom section confirms that static methods are insufficient. Removing <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Agentic Verification</span> entirely (w/o All) leads to a 21.7% drop in SRR. Specifically, <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Semantic Linking</span> proves most critical (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>14.2%), as the agent must first hypothesize column roles (e.g., foreign keys) to guide exploration. <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Table Exploration</span> is also vital (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>9.2%) for resolving ambiguities not addressed by metadata. Finally, <span id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Global Synthesis</span> contributes to robustness (<math id="S4.SS4.SSS3.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>4.2%) by ensuring the selected columns form a connected graph.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6. </span>Ablation study on SQL generation. The evaluation compares performance with and without the guidance module, reporting EX@8 for quality, and average exploration rounds (<math id="S4.T6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{R}}</annotation></semantics></math>) and query count (<math id="S4.T6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{Q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{Q}}</annotation></semantics></math>) per example for efficiency.</figcaption>

<th id="S4.T6.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:6.4pt;padding-right:6.4pt;" rowspan="2"><span id="S4.T6.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LLM</span></th>
<th id="S4.T6.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:6.4pt;padding-right:6.4pt;" rowspan="2"><span id="S4.T6.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Method</span></th>
<th id="S4.T6.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:6.4pt;padding-right:6.4pt;" colspan="3"><span id="S4.T6.2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spider 2.0-Snow (<math id="S4.T6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=120</annotation></semantics></math>)</span></th></tr>
<tr id="S4.T6.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S4.T6.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:6.4pt;padding-right:6.4pt;"><span id="S4.T6.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EX@8 (%)<math id="S4.T6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math></span></td>

<td id="S4.T6.2.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:6.4pt;padding-right:6.4pt;"><math id="S4.T6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{Q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{Q}}</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T6.2.3" class="ltx_tr">

<section id="S4.SS4.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.4.4. </span>Ablation Study on SQL Generation Components</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While Section <a href="#S4.SS4.SSS1" title="4.4.1. Effect of Exploration ‣ 4.4. Analysis ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4.1</span></a> demonstrates the impact of exploration, we now further isolate the contribution of the deterministic guidance module by comparing it against a baseline without directives.
We report EX@8 to remove the influence of answer selection. To quantify exploration efficiency, we define the average exploration rounds <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{R}}</annotation></semantics></math> and the average query count <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{Q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{Q}}</annotation></semantics></math> across <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> questions and <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=8</annotation></semantics></math> samples as:</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(6)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{R}}=\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathcal{R}_{i,j},\quad\bar{\mathcal{Q}}=\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathcal{Q}_{i,j}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{R}}=\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathcal{R}_{i,j},\quad\bar{\mathcal{Q}}=\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathcal{Q}_{i,j}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{i,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{i,j}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{Q}_{i,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒬</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Q}_{i,j}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the number of exploration rounds and total exploratory SQL queries generated for the i-<math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="th" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">th</annotation></semantics></math> sample in the j-<math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="th" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">th</annotation></semantics></math> run. As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Agentic Verification. ‣ 4.4.3. Ablation Study on Schema Linking Components ‣ 4.4. Analysis ‣ 4. Experiments ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, incorporating guidance consistently improves execution accuracy across all models (e.g., GPT-4o <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow 3.75\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><mrow><mn>3.75</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow 3.75\%</annotation></semantics></math>). This confirms that guidance helps the agent start with a stronger foundation, leading to more focused and efficient exploration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond performance gains, the guidance module streamlines the interaction process. Across all models, <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{R}</annotation></semantics></math> decreases when guidance is provided, indicating that fewer steps are needed to resolve uncertainties. Notably, while the number of rounds decreases, the total query count <math id="S4.SS4.SSS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{Q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{Q}</annotation></semantics></math> remains comparable or increases, suggesting that the agent performs more meaningful probes per interaction.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5. </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we present <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span>, an agentic framework shifting the Text-to-SQL paradigm from passive schema perception to agentic exploration. For schema linking, we combine logical planning with dual-pathway pruning to navigate massive search spaces, employing agentic exploration to ground column selection in empirical evidence. For SQL generation, we utilize deterministic retrieval to guide data profiling, allowing the agent to resolve implementation details and value ambiguities. Experiments on BIRD and Spider 2.0-Snow show that <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">APEX-SQL</span> outperforms competitive baselines. Analysis reveals that agentic exploration acts as a performance multiplier, particularly for stronger models, while deterministic guidance enhances effectiveness and efficiency. We conclude that equipping models to verify hypotheses against physical data is a highly effective mechanism for robust enterprise data analysis.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Instruction Templates</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section provides the instruction templates referenced in the main text. Each prompt corresponds to specific components of our framework, as detailed below:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{plan}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{plan}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{agg}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{agg}</annotation></semantics></math>: For Logical Planning in Section <a href="#S3.SS2.SSS1" title="3.2.1. Hypothesis Generation via Logical Planning ‣ 3.2. Agentic Exploration for Schema Linking ‣ 3. Methodology ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2.1</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{del}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{del}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{sl}_{sel}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{sl}_{sel}</annotation></semantics></math>: For Dual-Pathway Pruning in Section <a href="#S3.SS2.SSS2" title="3.2.2. Search Space Reduction via Dual-Pathway Pruning ‣ 3.2. Agentic Exploration for Schema Linking ‣ 3. Methodology ‣ APEX-SQL: Talking to the data via Agentic Exploration for Text-to-SQL" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2.2</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>

<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{schema}

<br class="ltx_break"></span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">*** EVIDENCE ***</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{evidence}

<br class="ltx_break"></span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">*** STRICT GUIDELINES ***</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. **High Recall (Safety)**:</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- If the column name is related to the query (even 1% chance), you should keep it. If not, check the desciption to see if it is related to the query. Sometimes the description is not clear, then you should pay close attention to the sample rows of the table. If the sample values of some columns are related to the query, you should keep these columns. If all of these information are not clear enough, remove it.</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. **Definition of Relevance**: Relevance includes both **Lexical Matching** and **Semantic Relatedness** over column name and description.</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Lexical**: If a word from the query appears in the name (e.g., query mentions "school" -&gt; keep ‘school_code‘, ‘school_type‘, etc.), it MUST be retained.</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Semantic**: Keep columns conceptually related to the topic. For example, if the query asks about "patents that were granted in …", then the column ‘grant_date‘ should be kept.</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.18" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.18.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **CRITICAL**: Do NOT remove discriminator columns such as ‘xxx_id‘, ‘xxx_name‘, ‘xxx_code‘, or ‘xxx_type‘ if the table itself is kept.</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.19" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.19.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. **Output Removal List**:</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.20" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.20.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Tables**: If a whole table is irrelevant, list it in ‘obviously_irrelevant_tables‘. Then all columns of that table will be kept. You do NOT need to list its columns separately.</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.21" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.21.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Columns**: If specific columns of a table are noise, list them in ‘obviously_irrelevant_columns‘.</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.22" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.22.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">4. **Grouped Tables**: If multiple tables are presented as sharing the same columns, you MUST list the removal instructions for **EACH** table explicitly. Pay close attention to name differences within the group (e.g., xx_2017 vs xx_2026), as these reflect specific data dimensions (like time) that determine relevance to the query.

<br class="ltx_break"></span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.23" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.23.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">*** OUTPUT FORMAT ***</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.24" class="ltx_p"><code id="A1.p5.pic1.2.24.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">```</code><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.24.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">json</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.25" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.25.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.26" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.26.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">"obviously_irrelevant_tables": ["table_unused_1", "table_unused_2"],</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.27" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.27.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">"obviously_irrelevant_columns": [</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.28" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.28.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">{</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.29" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.29.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">"table": "t1",</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.30" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.30.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">"columns": ["col_unused_1", "col_unused_2"]</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.31" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.31.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">}</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.32" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.32.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">]</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.33" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.33.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">}</span></span>
<span id="A1.p5.pic1.2.34" class="ltx_p"><code id="A1.p5.pic1.2.34.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">```</code></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
